Beautiful Views, Disappointing Food – A Really Bad Dining Experience at NEKTR The views at NEKTR are absolutely amazing, and the ambience is beautiful. Unfortunately, the food was nowhere close to what we expected, making it a very disappointing experience. Here’s what went wrong with almost everything we ordered: * Malai Broccoli: Loaded with cardamom and so sweet that it tasted more like a dessert than a savoury starter. * Chicken Coriander Soup: Just chicken broth with barely two tiny pieces of chicken. Extremely disappointing. * Tofu Tom Kha Soup: Essentially spicy coconut milk with just two micro-mini tofu dumplings. There was hardly anything substantial in it. * Dark Chocolate Mousse: The worst part of the meal. It tasted more like chocolate halwa than mousse, and to make matters worse, it wasn’t even served cold. The food was so disappointing that we eventually gave up on NEKTR and walked to the Biryani Zone in the next building for our main course. While the view is undoubtedly beautiful, a great ambience cannot compensate for such poor food quality and execution. We came expecting a wonderful dining experience but left thoroughly disappointed. NEKTR has a beautiful setting, but the food definitely needs serious improvement. Not an experience we would want to repeat.

Craving Punjabi soul food on the Bengaluru outskirts? 9th Mile Dhaba nailed it on our recent road trip! Tucked along the highway, this no-frills spot serves up dhaba magic that punches way above its weight. The star? Their Amritsari fish—crispy, golden-battered sole fried to flaky perfection, bursting with ajwain, ginger-garlic punch, and a tangy chaat masala kick. Paired with their buttery, tandoor-fresh naan (plain, garlic, or butter— all pillowy soft with charred edges), it was a match made in food heaven. Dipped in their spicy green chutney and onion rings, we devoured two plates guilt-free! Don’t skip the sides: creamy dal makhani simmered for hours, tandoori chicken that’s smoky and juicy, and lassi so thick and sweet it hits like dessert. Meals are hearty, fresh, and priced right (~₹300-500 for two). Service is lightning-fast despite the crowds, with unlimited refills on pickles and masala chai. Perfect pitstop for highway drives—rustic seating, breezy outdoors, and that unbeatable dhaba energy. If you’re near Yelahanka or heading to Nandi Hills, detour here NOW. Foodies, you’ve been warned: addiction ahead! 🐟🍞🔥

The rice was fragrant and cooked to perfection, but the meat left much to be desired. The mutton in the biryani was not properly cooked – it was tough and lacked the tenderness and flavor that one would expect in a biryani dish. While the rest of the dishes we ordered were decent, the mutton biryani's quality was a significant drawback for me. I believe that improving the preparation of the meat in this dish could make a substantial difference in the overall dining experience.

As diehard foodies, my partner and I are quite aware of the good restaurants in and around Bengaluru. We had been hearing a lot about the different outlets of ‘Kapoor’s Café.’ In fact, we spotted the Yelahanka outlet just opposite to ‘The Galleria Mall’ on quite a few occasions. That and the fact that many acquaintances have spoken well of the eatery inspired us to visit the Yelahanka outlet yesterday (Saturday – March 14, 2026). One look at the restaurant and we were quite impressed with the décor. The way different kinds of posters were hung showed that quite a bit of thoughts was put into the making of the café. Anyway, both of us went for the Thali options. While my partner ordered the ‘Matar Paneer Combo,’ I went ahead with the more experimental ‘Palak Paneer Combo.’ Alongside, we also ordered two (2) glasses of ‘Lassi Gur Wali’ and a bottle of the eatery’s own brand of drinking water. All the items on the two thalis were excellent. What impressed us the most was the ‘Lassi Gur Wali.’ It was nothing short of being magical. The taste was absolutely authentic. I could have had it anywhere in Punjab as well. Subject to the shortage of LPG Gas Cylinders, the thalis took a bit of time to arrive. Else, everything was simply spot on. The bill amount was also not that high. Overall, it was a very satisfactory experience for both of us. In the future, we would like to visit the other outlets of the eatery. Cheers!

On the positive side, the food is tasty, the restaurant attracts a good crowd, parking is plentiful, and it stays open until late at night. My verdict: Thamaq has the food and location to attract customers, but the staff needs proper training in hospitality, service etiquette and basic table hygiene. Packaged food and sweets: 5 star. .They've got a very wide range of sweets and packaged food, which is already a plus. The video of their factory and hygiene standards on YouTube assures you're not buying something poorly made. Almost on par with Haldirams (haldirams being slightly better). 5. Dinner choices in the first floor were not that great and cost higher than average prices. They were just OK enough. 6. The room (think it was called deluxe and was room no. 1) was not that good. While the price seemed alright and the room was quite spacious, there were food stains on the bedsheets, the floor had dirt, the bathroom and room in general was very outdated. It did include a mini tiffin breakfast which was kind of worth it. 7. Similar situation with the restaurant as well. There's some smell you get from frequently used cleaning cloths. The washroom needs big improvement. 8. Parking is still a minor concern during rush hour though there's enough now that the adjacent land (previously Lamborghini service centre) has opened up and there's some more parking under the metro bridge. 9. Reachability and location is quite good for those arriving or departing from/to the airport. Overall. A relatively decent place for south Indian food in the area as an alternative to "Hotel Shivaprasad Veg" near the Toll Gate for South and North Indian veg food with the bonus of packed sweets and snacks.

⭐ 1/5 — Extremely disappointing breakfast buffet I normally never write bad reviews for restaurants, but my experience at Itihas today was bad enough that I genuinely felt people should know before spending their money here. I went for the non-veg breakfast buffet, which was around ₹300. The price itself isn’t the issue — you can charge ₹300, ₹600, or even ₹800, but the quality of the food should at least be acceptable. The fish had a very unpleasant smell, and the chicken was honestly one of the worst-tasting chicken dishes I’ve ever had. The overall quality of the food was extremely disappointing. There was dosa, set dosa and a few other items, but the buffet had very little variety, and there wasn’t even a basic juice option. Calling this a breakfast buffet feels misleading when the selection is so limited and the food quality is this poor. It’s not about the price; it’s about value and basic food quality. If the restaurant wants to charge more, that’s completely fine — make it ₹600 or ₹800, but serve food that is actually worth eating. Unfortunately, based on today’s experience, I won’t be visiting Itihas again, and I would strongly suggest checking the buffet before committing to it.

We recently placed a bulk order at this restaurant for our team of 15, planning ahead for a smooth evening dinner pickup after a long workday. I called a full day in advance to place the order, large varieties and generous quantities, including chicken biryani as the highlight, with portions calculated for 20 people to ensure everyone got plenty. We even followed up with another call 30 minutes before arriving, confirming we'd be there shortly. Despite all this foresight, we ended up waiting nearly an hour just to get our hands on the food. The staff seemed completely unprepared, scrambling around as if it was a last-minute walk-in. To make matters worse, quality was shockingly subpar. Several chicken biryani packets arrived with zero chicken pieces, just plain rice pretending to be biryani. Portions across the board were laughably small; what was meant to feed 20 barely stretched to our group of 15, forcing us to supplement with cafeteria leftovers to avoid hungry teammates. The veg curries were drowned in watery gravy that tasted identical to the chicken gravy, no distinct flavors, just bland mush. They even swapped promised chicken dishes with random paneer, kaju, and vegetable kurma without a heads-up or apology, leaving us short on protein for a meat-heavy order. Pricing felt like a total rip-off for such meager, disappointing quantities way overpriced compared to nearby spots that deliver reliably. Food taste? Strictly average at best, nothing memorable or crave-worthy. Service was the real dealbreaker: disorganized, unresponsive, and utterly poor from start to finish. Save your time, money, and frustration, plenty of better restaurants nearby nail bulk orders without the hassle. Won't be back, and I strongly advise steering clear. 1/5 stars.

After landing back in Bangalore from Pune around 11:15 PM, we headed to Empire Restaurant in Devanahalli for a late-night family dinner. When it comes to late-night dining in and around Bangalore, Empire is always a safe and reliable choice. We reached the restaurant around 12:15 AM, and although they had already sold out of their famous biryani (which wasn't surprising at that hour!), the rest of the food was absolutely delicious. We ordered Alfaham Chicken, Pepper Chicken, Pepper Brain Fry, Parottas with Chicken Curry, and Ghee Rice. Every dish was fresh, flavorful, and served hot. The Pepper Brain Fry was excellent, the Alfaham Chicken was perfectly grilled, and the Ghee Rice was as aromatic and delicious as ever. One thing I truly appreciate about Empire is the consistency they maintain across all their branches. Whether it's the quality of the food, the quick service, or the overall experience, they rarely disappoint—even well past midnight. Overall, we had a satisfying late-night dinner with our family after a long journey. If you're looking for authentic Muslim-style food around Devanahalli, especially late at night, Empire is a place you can count on. Highly recommended!

The Empire non-veg thali is a filling and value-for-money meal with a good mix of flavours and textures. It comes with soft rice topped with a crisp papad and a flaky parotta that pairs well with the gravies, along with a mildly spiced, comforting dal that balances the heavier items. On the non-veg side, the fried chicken is crispy outside and fairly juicy inside, the chilli chicken delivers a spicy masala kick with capsicum and onions, and the chicken curry has a thick, rich gravy that works well with both rice and parotta. Portions are generous, sides and pickles add extra punch, and the lemon mint cooler was refreshing and really good, cutting through the richness of the meal. Overall, it’s slightly on the heavier side as expected from Empire, but still a satisfying and worthwhile choice for non-veg lovers when you’re really hungry.

Location & Access: Situated just north of Devanahalli town, this spot is easy to catch on your right when driving out of Bengaluru toward Hyderabad on NH 44. Since it sits on the opposite side of the highway, you will need to take a quick U-turn right after the main traffic signal. There is plenty of dedicated parking space out front, making pulling in hassle-free. Space & Ambience: The property is massive. Along with a spacious air-conditioned dining hall, they also have a neat lawn area out back that looks well-suited for small gatherings or private parties. What immediately stands out is the upkeep—the entire dining area is spotless, fresh-smelling, and even the washrooms are remarkably clean, which is always a huge plus on a highway drive. Food & Fresh Juices: We stopped here around 9:00 AM. As is standard across most South Indian highway eateries at that hour, only the South Indian breakfast menu was available. Everything was served piping hot within 15 to 20 minutes. A special shout-out goes to their fruit juices: they are freshly squeezed with no preservatives or added sugar—something that is both rare at highway stops and genuinely commendable. Service & Pricing: The staff is polite, patient, and attentive when taking orders. Pricing is fair and well-aligned with the portion sizes and taste. Verdict: A solid, reliable highway pitstop. Between the clean washrooms, ample parking, and hot breakfast, it is well worth pulling over for if you are heading out on NH 44.

Koteshwaram – The Temple of Divine Food is a wonderful place to stop for a satisfying and delicious meal, especially if you are traveling on the highway. Located conveniently along the highway, it is easy to access and makes for a perfect break during long journeys. The moment you enter, the place feels clean, spacious, and well-organized, with a calm and welcoming atmosphere that suits families, travelers, and groups alike. The food here is truly impressive, and the highlight of my visit was the masala dosa. It was absolutely delicious — crisp on the outside, soft inside, and cooked to perfection. The potato masala was well-spiced, flavorful, and tasted fresh. The dosa was served hot with a generous portion of chutney and sambar, both of which complemented the dosa very well. The coconut chutney was fresh and aromatic, and the sambar had a rich, authentic South Indian taste. Every bite felt satisfying and comforting. Apart from the masala dosa, the overall menu offers a good variety of vegetarian dishes, making it suitable for breakfast, lunch, or even an early dinner stop. The quality of ingredients is clearly maintained, and the food tastes hygienic and freshly prepared. Portion sizes are good, and the pricing feels reasonable for the quality and location. The service is quick and efficient, which is especially important for highway travelers. The staff are polite and attentive, ensuring orders are served promptly even during busy hours. The restaurant and washroom areas are clean and well-maintained, adding to the overall positive experience. Overall, Koteshwaram – The Temple of Divine Food lives up to its name. Great taste, especially the masala dosa, convenient highway location, good service, and a clean environment make it a 5-star experience for me. I would definitely stop here again and highly recommend it to anyone traveling along this route. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

TLDR: Discover the ultimate pit stop with endless parking, stunning gardens, and a dining experience that caters to everyone! From gourmet fine dining to quick Darshini bites, indulge in crispy dosas with perfect fillings, a delightful surprise of two bondas in soup, and creamy, fresh coffee. Enjoy friendly staff and a relaxing atmosphere that lets you unwind long after your meal. Don’t miss out on this hidden gem! The eatery offers ample parking space, making it an ideal pit stop for travelers. It features a well-maintained front yard garden that adds to its charm. For those looking to spend quality time, there are options for fine dining, providing an elegant and comfortable atmosphere. On the other hand, for quick travelers, there is a traditional self-service Darshini type setup, perfect for grabbing a quick coffee or simply using the washroom facilities. Speaking of washrooms, the eatery has thoughtfully categorized them into men’s, women’s, disabled, and diaper-changing rooms, ensuring convenience for all visitors. However, the only drawback is that these facilities are located at the far end of the eatery, which might be a bit inconvenient for some. During our visit, we indulged in the benne masala dose or also more as the butter masala dosa. It was cooked to perfection, with a crispy exterior and a soft interior. The aloo filling was seasoned with just the right amount of saltiness, and the accompanying chutney and sambhar complemented the dosas beautifully, creating a harmonious blend of flavors. We also tried the bonda soup, which was a delightful surprise. Typically, one bonda is served, but we were pleasantly surprised to receive two. While I expected it to be a bit spicier and more peppery, it was still incredibly delicious and satisfying. To conclude our evening snack, we enjoyed a cup of coffee that was creamy and fresh, perfectly hitting the right spots and leaving us refreshed. The staff at the eatery were exceptionally friendly and welcoming. They did not rush us to leave even after we had settled the bill, allowing us to relax and decompress on the property. Overall, it was a wonderful experience, and we had a great time enjoying the food and ambiance.

We went to this Samara Veg especially for breakfast at the Chikkaballapur branch. We had previously visited their other outlet, around 40 km further ahead, and had an amazing experience, so we decided to drive from Bengaluru to try this one as well. Thankfully, this branch did not disappoint either! I really appreciated the thoughtful little touches here — mint lemon water, a wheelchair ramp, a mini washbasin for kids in the washroom, and a kids’ play area. These may seem like small things, but they make the place feel much more welcoming and family-friendly. The food was tasty and lived up to our expectations. We ordered Pongal, masala dosa, rava idli, kesari bath, tea, and jaggery coffee. The Pongal was different from what is usually served at their other outlet, but in a refreshing and delicious way. The masala dosa was slightly cold, but still tasty. Rava idli was good, and the kesari bath was absolutely delicious. The tea was a little too sweet for my liking, but otherwise tasted good. The jaggery coffee was a nice addition. It had a good coffee flavour without being overly sweet, so the sweetness didn’t overpower the coffee. The washrooms were clean, and the overall place was hygienic, well-maintained, and thoughtfully designed. The only area that could be improved is the service speed. Placing the order and sometimes having to repeat it can get a little frustrating. However, once the order is placed correctly, the food is served quite quickly. Overall, it was definitely worth the drive from Bengaluru. A nice place for a family breakfast, with good food, clean surroundings, and some thoughtful touches that make the experience better. Would happily visit again! If you want, I can also make this **shorter and more punchy for a Google review**, while keeping the same points.
